The Bool-valued check is a closed-form certificate generator: `multiplicity n d ≤ 2` on every chord-distance class d ∈ [1, ⌊n/2⌋] certifies the premise for EVERY centre x_i and EVERY radius r > 0 (each vertex-to-vertex distance is realized by at most 2 other vertices, so no circle centred at a vertex contains 3 other points — the contract's problem-specific trap is discharged by the all-radii argument, not by checking special radii); `(List.range (n/2)).length = ⌊n/2⌋` is the exact distinct-distance count D = ⌊n/2⌋; and `2·⌊n/2⌋ ≤ n < (1+c)·n` for every real c > 0 gives the strict violation D

minimal witnesses (3,2) and (2,2) both violate n≥2k (n<2k), so the certified-census claim is false on the canonical domain; first admissible k=2 pair is (6,2) with deficiency 0; repair requires domain-exact census plus explicit B(k) and proved finite-core transfer

explicit 4-periodic walk over S={e1,e2} satisfies all frozen premises yet its four-point image (unit square vertices) has no three collinear points; canonical statement is false as frozen and must be re-frozen with an injectivity/unboundedness premise before either branch can close nontrivially
Oscillating walk with S={±(1,0,0)} visits only 2 distinct points, refuting the statement as frozen; repair requires an infinite-distinct-points hypothesis or an explicit distinctness convention.

REFUTED by external audit (GPT gold-mine audit + R4, 2026-09-01), each item re-verified by the operator's session against the frozen contract or by exact computation on 2026-09-02 | FALSE: Pintz/Rankin-type results concern LARGE GAPS between consecutive primes, not the length of arithmetic progressions of primes in [1,N]. No theorem gives L(N) = omega(log N) infinitely often; the longest known prime APs in [1,N] have length far below log N and the o(log N) question is open. 'negative close achieved' is a citation misuse.
